title: Discovery: Embeddings + Reranking - CatalystSearch
summary: Initial discovery to understand CatalystSearch's search stack and requirements for embeddings + reranking. Key concerns: vector DB compatibility, throughput for 10M+ vectors, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, hybrid search with BM25, and security/compliance requirements for customer data. Redwood AE/SE outlined Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and proposed a POC: 10M vectors, 2-week benchmark, cross-encoder rerank evaluation. Next step: send pricing options, security docs, and schedule technical deep dive next week.
topics: throughput and tail latency for 10M+ vectors
embedding dimensionality (1536 vs 768) and cost tradeoffs
hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings) and reranking architecture
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, data residency
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated vs Hosted pricing sheet by 2027-01-13
Send security whitepaper and SOC2 report to Priya by 2027-01-13
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive to run POC benchmarks (10M vectors) week of 2027-01-18
Provide suggested model/dimension profile and estimated token cost for reranking flow
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pricing and Dedicated capacity options (due 2027-01-13)

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya, Diego (Redwood); Sophie, Liam, Priya (CatalystSearch)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery: CatalystSearch evaluating embeddings + rerank integration. Looking for throughput on 10M vectors, hybrid search, and security posture.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm maya from redwood, and with me is diego, our solutions engineer. how's it going?
[00:07] Sophie Patel: hi maya, hi diego. good, thanks. we—i'm sophie, head of search at catalystsearch. we run product search and site search for e-commerce clients.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: liam here, ml eng. been building our embedding pipeline and working on rerank.
[00:19] Priya Rao: priya, security. i'll be evaluating compliance and contracts.
[00:23] Maya Chen: great. quick agenda: 1) current stack and pain, 2) throughput and scale needs, 3) redwood options (hosted/dedicated/private), 4) next steps. sound ok?
[00:30] Sophie Patel: yup, sounds good. to start, our current stack is opensearch for first-pass BM25, pinecone for vector store experiments, and a small cross-encoder reranker on CPU for final ranking. main pain is inconsistent latency under load and ops overhead maintaining pinecone indexes across clients.
[00:49] Diego Alvarez: ok, thanks. when you say inconsistent latency, can you quantify p95/p99 and typical qps?
[00:55] Liam O'Connor: right now baseline qps is 250 steady, spikes to 1k during sales events. p95 for embedding retrieval is around 180ms, p99 creeps to 700ms which kills our SLAs. reranker adds another 200-400ms depending on batch.
[01:13] Maya Chen: got it. and data size? how many vectors and dims?
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: we're at ~12M vectors across multi-tenant indexes. dims are mixed, but production embeddings we're testing are 1536 from open models. we did try 768 and saw slight accuracy drop, but cost savings — it's a tradeoff.
[01:32] Sophie Patel: and we run hybrid search—bm25 first-pass, then embed ANN, then cross-encoder rerank for top 20. our cost on reranker is material.
[01:42] Diego Alvarez: ok so sounds like two main knobs: reduce retrieval latency and reduce reranker cost. for retrieval, redwood can offer optimized serving paths and Dedicated pools for predictable throughput. for rerank we typically suggest a two-stage approach: cheap embed rerank first then cross-encoder on top N.
[02:00] Liam O'Connor: we do similar. question on vector DB integration: how compatible is Redwood with pinecone/milvus/weaviate or do you expect us to migrate to yours?
[02:09] Maya Chen: good q. Redwood Hosted exposes a standard embeddings API — you can keep vector DB as your index, we return embedding vectors that you can push into pinecone or milvus. For Dedicated/Private, we can co-locate an ANN service and provide an integrated index (FAISS-based) so you don't need separate provider. integration is flexible.
[02:27] Priya Rao: from security side, for Dedicated or Private deployments, is there KMS/HSM integration and audit logs? we need SSO with SAML and long retention for logs.
[02:37] Diego Alvarez: yes — Private includes customer-managed KMS and audit log export. Dedicated has encrypted at rest and optional KMS integration, plus per-token traceability in the console. we'll share the SOC2 report and whitepaper after this call.
[02:50] Sophie Patel: awesome. what about throughput? for 12M vectors we need low p99 and steady qps—what's realistic for hosted vs dedicated?
[02:59] Diego Alvarez: for Hosted we have multi-tenant limits; typical p95 around 80-120ms for retrieval on smaller datasets but tail depends on vector size and search config. Dedicated gives predictable capacity — we can size GPU pools for your qps and target p99 under 200ms for retrieval at 1k qps with sharding and optimized ANN (quantization + IVFPQ or HNSW tuning).
[03:21] Liam O'Connor: you mentioned quantization—does that affect accuracy? we care about recall at top 10 for product search.
[03:27] Diego Alvarez: yes slightly. with 8-bit or product quantization you can get 1–3% drop in recall depending on model/dims, but massive speedups and memory savings. we typically recommend testing 1536->quantized profile vs 768 dense to measure the real tradeoff on your dataset.
[03:44] Sophie Patel: can redwood host the reranker model too? we have a cross-encoder that is custom and privacy-sensitive.
[03:51] Maya Chen: Hosted can host models but for very sensitive models we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control model artifacts and networking. Private on-prem gives full isolation. Dedicated is a good middle ground with VPC peering and customer-managed keys.
[04:05] Liam O'Connor: for reranking, are there best practices to reduce cost — like batching or running smaller cross-encoders?
[04:11] Diego Alvarez: yes batching helps but cross-encoders are expensive by nature. common patterns: 1) use a lightweight bi-encoder for initial rerank of top 200 -> top 50, 2) only run cross-encoder on top 20 results, 3) cache rerank outputs for frequent queries, 4) use per-route SLOs to avoid reranking cold traffic. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quantization and caching config for your workload.
[04:34] Sophie Patel: curious — model dims. our engineering prefers 1536 embeddings for accuracy, but cost team pushes for 768. what's the practical delta for ecomm product search?
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: varies by dataset. we often see diminishing returns beyond 1536 for product titles + metadata. For some catalogs 768 hits 90–95% of the metric and is half memory/cpu cost. we recommend running a small ablation during POC: 1M vectors at both dims to measure recall@10 and latency/cost.
[05:05] Priya Rao: latency SLA question — if we pick Hosted and we hit a region outage, are there fallbacks?
[05:11] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood provides smart routing: requests can failover to alternate region or to lower-cost model variant if capacity constrained. for strict SLAs we advise Dedicated with multi-zone redundancy.
[05:22] Sophie Patel: how would we do hybrid search practically? currently BM25 first-pass then embed ANN. any recommended architecture changes?
[05:30] Diego Alvarez: that flow is common. Another approach is score fusion — combine BM25 and ANN scores then rerank. The main engineering challenge is keeping candidate sets balanced. Also consider using lightweight filters (category, availability) pre-ANN to reduce unnecessary calls.
[05:46] Liam O'Connor: for the POC, we want to simulate sales-event traffic and replay real query distribution. what infra will redwood need?
[05:55] Diego Alvarez: for a benchmark we'll need sample queries, a snapshot of vectors (anonymized), and target qps profile. We'll recommend a Dedicated pool config to match the spikes and run tests with different ANN configs and quantizations.
[06:08] Sophie Patel: what's the expected timeline for a POC?
[06:11] Maya Chen: typically 2–3 weeks of setup + 1 week of benchmarking and analysis. total 3–4 weeks. we can compress if urgent.
[06:18] Priya Rao: can we keep logs and data within our GCP region? data residency is a hard requirement for some clients.
[06:23] Maya Chen: Private or Dedicated can be region-locked. Hosted can restrict region but multi-tenant backups might cross region — for compliance we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[06:34] Liam O'Connor: ok, question on embedding generation: do you recommend running embeddings in our infra or use Redwood embedding API?
[06:40] Diego Alvarez: both are valid. If you want reduced latency and control, host embeddings locally and push vectors to index. If you want simpler ops, Redwood Hosted embeddings API can generate vectors and handle model updates. For PII-sensitive data, do embedding locally then send vectors to Redwood if using Dedicated/Private with encryption.
[07:00] Sophie Patel: cost-wise, can you ballpark monthly for 12M vectors with 1536 dims on Dedicated? rough order.
[07:08] Maya Chen: rough order depends on sharding and replication. I'll put a conservative estimate in the pricing sheet, but ballpark — with GPU-backed ANN and moderate replication you're looking at mid-five to low-six figures per month; Hosted will be lower to start but less predictable at scale. We'll send detailed numbers.
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: sounds like we need to set clear success criteria for POC — recall@10 >= current baseline, p99 retrieval under 300ms at 1k qps, rerank cost under X.
[07:36] Maya Chen: agreed. we'll propose success criteria in the POC plan.
[07:40] Sophie Patel: any constraints around index updates? our catalog changes frequently — add/delete ~50k vectors per day.
[07:47] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated/Private supports near-real-time updates; we handle incremental indexing and shard rebalancing. There is an operational cost for high write volume; we'll size the cluster accordingly.
[07:59] Priya Rao: on contracts, we'll likely require a DPA and specific SLAs. we'll share the legal points.
[08:05] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll loop in legal after this.
[08:08] Sophie Patel: on evaluation metrics, we also care about tail latency during retrain or reindex jobs; those often spike. any recommended isolation?
[08:17] Diego Alvarez: we recommend separate indexing pipelines and throttling or schedule heavy reindex jobs off-peak. With Dedicated you can set separate capacity for indexing nodes to avoid interfering with query-serving pools.
[08:29] Liam O'Connor: related — can redwood do on-the-fly quantization or do we need to rebuild indexes?
[08:35] Diego Alvarez: some quantization can be applied post-hoc with little downtime; others require rebuilds. we'll detail the expected downtime in the POC plan per method.
[08:46] Sophie Patel: any customers in retail/ecommerce with similar scale?
[08:50] Maya Chen: yes — we have references (anonymized) in mid-market ecomm; will include references in follow-up.
[08:57] Priya Rao: ok good. can you also share details around RBAC and per-route permissions?
[09:02] Diego Alvarez: yes, RBAC with role scoping and tokenized access is available; Dedicated/Private supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll include docs.
[09:12] Sophie Patel: one more thing — does Redwood provide an integrated ANN index or do we manage indexes ourselves? you touched on this but want specifics.
[09:20] Maya Chen: for Hosted you manage index in your vector DB (we provide vectors + SDK). For Dedicated we can provide managed ANN (FAISS/HNSW) that we operate for you with options to export snapshots. Private gives you full control on-prem.
[09:33] Liam O'Connor: good. for reranker model hosting — we have a custom cross-encoder that cannot leave our environment, is it possible to run reranker on-prem and just call Redwood for retrieval?
[09:43] Diego Alvarez: absolutely — you can run retrieval via Redwood and call your on-prem reranker for final scoring. Many customers use hybrid patterns where retrieval is outsourced and rerank stays in-house.
[09:53] Sophie Patel: ok, sounds flexible.
[09:56] Maya Chen: great. let's talk concrete POC scope — we propose: 1) ingest 10M vectors (anonymized snapshot), 2) run retrieval benchmarks at 1k qps with traffic spikes to 1.5k, 3) test 1536 vs 768 and 8-bit quantized profiles, 4) measure rerank cost with top 20 cross-encoder run on batch sizes X, 5) produce report with recommended deployment (Dedicated vs Private).
[10:18] Liam O'Connor: that's good. what infra will you provision for that?
[10:21] Diego Alvarez: we'll propose a Dedicated pool: n1 GPUs with sharding and a separate indexing node. specifics in the POC plan.
[10:29] Priya Rao: can you confirm data handling? we'll only send anonymized vectors for testing but need clarity on log retention and who has access.
[10:36] Maya Chen: yes, we'll document access controls; for Dedicated we restrict access to your account techs + redwood on-call if needed; logs can be exported to your GCS/S3.
[10:47] Sophie Patel: ok. question on cost modelling — do you provide token-level cost for reranker calls? we need that for forecasting.
[10:54] Maya Chen: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown, per-route cost, and a cost projection tool. We'll share a sample export.
[11:02] Liam O'Connor: nice. any gotchas with hybrid search and category filters? we currently apply category filters pre-ANN which helps reduce noise.
[11:10] Diego Alvarez: that's good practice. also consider using metadata HNSW filters (if supported) to avoid false positives. We'll test with your data.
[11:18] Sophie Patel: perfect. anything else?
[11:20] Maya Chen: i think we're aligned. i'll summarize next steps: share pricing, security docs, POC plan, and schedule tech deep dive.
[11:27] Sophie Patel: yes please. we want the technical deep dive with diego next week — maybe 2027-01-19?
[11:33] Maya Chen: diego, you available?
[11:35] Diego Alvarez: yep, 19th looks open for me.
[11:38] Priya Rao: i'll be out but can join follow-up on compliance call.
[11:41] Sophie Patel: ok, send calendar invites.
[11:44] Maya Chen: will do. final quick Q: are there any licensing constraints if we use redwood-managed ANN indexes for client-owned models?
[11:52] Diego Alvarez: we'll include licensing terms in the DPA; generally we support customer-owned models and can host them under Dedicated/Private with contractual protections.
[12:02] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[12:05] Sophie Patel: thanks.
[12:06] Priya Rao: thanks.
[12:08] Maya Chen: bye all — we'll follow up with notes.

End of transcript.
